title: Regular expressions and the pumping lemma
subtitle: A notation for exactly the languages finite automata recognise — and a test for what they cannot.

re.title: Regular expressions
re.body: Regular expressions describe languages with three operators: union a|b (or +), concatenation ab, star a*. Examples over {0,1}: (0|1)*01 = ends in 01; 1*(01*01*)*… = even number of 0s. A language is regular exactly when a regular expression, a DFA, or an NFA describes it (Kleene’s theorem).

conv.title: From expression to automaton
conv.body: Build the ε-NFA piece by piece (Thompson): a single symbol is two states joined by that symbol; union adds a new start with ε-arrows to both machines; concatenation links the first’s accept to the second’s start by ε; star adds ε-loops and a bypass. The pieces are machines you can run — the one below is the result for a*b.
conv.steps: Does a*b accept aaab? Follow the loops on a, then b to the accepting state. Yes: a a a loop in s, b moves to f and the input ends there.

closure.title: Closure properties
closure.body: Regular languages are closed under union, concatenation, star, complement (swap accepting and non-accepting states of a DFA), intersection (product construction) and reversal. Closure gives proofs by construction: if L is regular then so is “strings in L that are not of even length”.

pump.title: The pumping lemma
pump.body: If L is regular there is a length p such that any string s ∈ L with |s| ≥ p can be split s = xyz with |xy| ≤ p, |y| ≥ 1, and xyⁱz ∈ L for every i ≥ 0. Why: a DFA with p states reading p symbols must repeat a state (pigeonhole), so the loop between can be repeated or removed. To prove L is not regular, pick a string that cannot be pumped.
pump.steps: Claim: L = {aⁿbⁿ} is not regular. Suppose it were, with pumping length p; take s = aᵖbᵖ. Since |xy| ≤ p, y consists only of a’s. Pumping up (i = 2) gives more a’s than b’s. So L is not regular — it needs to count, which a finite memory cannot.

decide.title: Decision algorithms
decide.body: For regular languages most questions are decidable by algorithm: is L empty (is an accepting state reachable?), finite, equal to another language (minimise both DFAs; compare), does a string belong (just run it).

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Regular expression ⇔ NFA ⇔ DFA.
  • Closed under union, concatenation, star, complement, intersection.
  • Pumping lemma shows non-regularity (aⁿbⁿ).
